unit.label: impl-front
unit.files: src/luthier/lexer.py, parser.py, syntax.py, pretty.py, api.py, and src/luthier/core.lut

sections: src/luthier/syntax.py (all 327 lines; AST nodes, mostly internal)

spec read against them: docs/semantica/02-grammar.md sections 1-8; 04-kernel.md sections 0-7; 05-static-semantics.md sections 0-7 (R1-R11), 9, 10; 06-numbers.md sections 2, 5, 6, 8; 03-libraries.md sections 2-4; 08-tests.md sections 0, 1, 3, 12, 13; 00-fundamental-elements.md sections 3-4
documentation: README.md (syntax, core.lut list, CLI lines 78-86) and a copy of examples/z7ring.lut (checks and evaluates as documented)
tests mapped: tests/spec/*.lut via tests/test_spec.py, tests/test_kernel.py, test_sugar.py, test_bridge.py, test_checker_rules.py, test_certificates.py, test_evaluators.py

behaviors.behavior: A closing ), ], >, or the } of a lambda, match or data, placed at column 0 on its own line is a parse error; it works only when indented. Record braces are the exception (parser.py:612, 655).
behaviors.spec_ref: 02-grammar.md:26-28 (inside ( ), [ ], < > and the braces of match and of a lambda, line breaks are ignored)

behaviors.behavior: A line break never separates the fields of a record value: the value is parsed with newlines skipped, so the next field name becomes an argument of the previous value.
behaviors.evidence: parser.py:608 sets skip_newlines = saved + 1 before parse_term, so `1` then `b` parse as application; the branch `if self.at("name"): continue` at parser.py:619 is unreachable. `P = { a : Int, b : Int }\np : P := { a := 1\n          b := 2 }` gives `parse error: line 3, col 12: expected another field or '}' in a record literal (at ':=')`; with a comma it evaluates `p.b` to 2. Record types do accept the line break (parser.py:632-648).

behaviors.behavior: Clauses are accepted only when the header has no := body; a body plus clauses is rejected ('definition has both a body and clauses'); clauses need parameters ('clauses need parameters in the header') and one pattern per parameter ('clause has N patterns but the header has M parameters', with no position).
behaviors.evidence:
parser.py:246-251 and 287-288. The grammar requires ':=' body before clauses; the parser requires its absence. `dbl (n : N) : N := zero
  | zero := zero ...` gives `parse error: line 6, col 0: definition has both a body and clauses (at '')` (reported at end of file); `dbl (n : N) : N
  | zero := zero
  | succ k := succ (succ (dbl k))`, which the grammar does not derive, evaluates `dbl (succ zero)` to `succ (succ zero)`. The test uses the body-less form.

behaviors.behavior: A subtype whose binder is a pattern, `{ (a, b) : Int * Int | a < b }`, is a parse error: only names are accepted before ':' in braces.
behaviors.evidence: parse_brace starts with self.expect("name") (parser.py:628). `Ord2 : U := { (a, b) : Int * Int | a < b }` gives `parse error: line 1, col 14: expected 'name', got '('`. The labeled form `{ a b : Int | a < b }` is the only way to bind several components.

behaviors.behavior: Explicit parentheses are not kept in the syntax tree, so the checker flattens `(A * B) * C` to `A * (B * C)` and `(A + B) + C` to `A + (B + C)`; a left-nested product or sum type cannot be written with * or +. Arithmetic stays left-associative.
behaviors.spec_ref: 04-kernel.md:74-76 (A * B * C is A * (B * C)); 02-grammar.md:62 (& and -> to the right, the others to the left)
behaviors.evidence: parser.py:579-581 returns the inner term; checker.py:1299-1305 and 1315-1321 flatten every nested BinOp '+' or '*'. `t : (Int * Bool) * String := ((1, true), "a")` gives `type error: in t: (1, true) has type Int * Bool but Int was expected`; `S = (Int + Bool) + String` then `s : S := left (left 3)` is rejected. Through an alias it works: `AB = Int * Bool`, `t : AB * String := ((1, true), "a")` evaluates. `24 / 4 / 2` is 3 (left). The two spec lines also disagree on * and + over types.

behaviors.behavior: Inside `< ... >`, a '>' always closes the union, even inside a nested subtype or parentheses, so an alternative whose type contains a '>' comparison cannot be written.
behaviors.evidence: _at_op refuses '>' and '|' while in_angle > 0 (parser.py:354); parse_paren resets no_brace but not in_angle (515), parse_brace resets neither (598-602). `T = < pos : { x : Int | x > 0 } | zero : Unit >` gives `parse error: line 1, col 26: expected '}', got '>'`; with `(x > 0)` it gives `expected ')', got '>'`; `0 < x` works.

behaviors.behavior: `operator op := f` accepts any symbol or keyword and `mod` (not `and`/`or`). `==`, `<`, `mod` then take effect, so `operator ==` gives == to a type that holds a function; `operator &`, `operator if`, `operator (` are accepted and do nothing.
behaviors.evidence: parser.py:149 only rejects tokens that are neither symbol nor keyword. With `P = { a : Int, f : Int -> Int }`, p and q of type P, `luthier eval f.lut "p == q"` gives `error: no structural equality on (a : Int) * (Int -> Int) ... (05 R8)`; adding `eqP (u v : P) : Bool := u.a == v.a` and `operator == := eqP` makes it `false : Bool`. `operator & := f`, `operator if := f`, `operator ( := f` all pass `luthier check`; `p & q` still says `left side of '&' is not a law`. The test covers + and * only.

behaviors.behavior: A float literal beyond the doubles becomes infinity and is accepted as a value of Float64 (`1e400` is `inf : Float64`); a literal below the smallest double silently becomes 0.0.
behaviors.spec_ref: 06-numbers.md:47-48 (infinities and NaN are not values of Float64); 08-tests.md:162; core.lut:21-22
behaviors.evidence: Lit(float(t.text)) with no range check. `big : Float64 := 1e400` passes `luthier check` and `luthier eval f.lut "big"` prints `inf : Float64`; `1e400 - 1e400` then fails with `NaN in inf - inf`; `1e-400` prints `0.0 : Float64`. tests/test_kernel.py:504 covers overflow from arithmetic only.

behaviors.behavior: A string literal in a term is decoded with Python's unicode_escape over its UTF-8 bytes, which corrupts non-ASCII text and processes backslash escapes; a string literal in a pattern is taken raw (parser.py:761). A pattern never matches the same literal written as a term when it has a non-ASCII character or an escape.
behaviors.evidence: `s : String := "café"` evaluates to `'cafÃ©' : String`; `len : String -> Int := extern "python:builtins.len"` gives `len "café"` = 5. `k (s : String) : Int := match s { "café" -> 1 ; _ -> 0 }` gives `k "café"` = 0, and with `"a\nb"` also 0, while `"abc"` gives 1. Same through luthier.load(...).eval. lib/table.lut:98,134 relies on escapes in terms.

behaviors.behavior: Program.fill does not apply R5 or R2 to the hole's type: it fills a type hole (`Session : U`) with a Python object, and a hole over a type that is only declared.
behaviors.spec_ref: 05-static-semantics.md:173-178 (R5: an extern gives a value, never a type; R2 applies to externs); 05-static-semantics.md:150-154 (R2)
behaviors.evidence: api.py:80-94 checks only 'is a hole' and arity. `Session : U` loaded, `P.fill("Session", list)` succeeds and the body becomes `Extern(target='fill:Session', type=U)`; `P.eval("Session")` then fails `cannot marshal Python value [] into Luthier type U`. `Signal : U\nduration : Signal -> Int`, then `P.fill("duration", len)` is accepted, while the same body in a file, tests/spec/r5_extern_over_declared.reject.lut, is rejected with 'Signal is used as a type but is only declared'. Probe: scratchpad/audit/impl-front/api_probe.py.

behaviors.behavior: Program.fill adds an obligation only when the hole's type is itself a subtype. A refined codomain, a record component or an array entry owes nothing, so a wrong Python filling cannot fail `test`.
behaviors.spec_ref: 05-static-semantics.md:179-187 (every refinement in the type of an extern is an obligation: codomain of each arrow, each component, each entry)
behaviors.evidence: api.py:95-101 calls subtype_obligation only if whnf(type) is a Subtype. `NonNeg : U := { x : Float64 | x >= 0.0 }\nneg : Float64 -> NonNeg`, `P.fill("neg", lambda x: -1.0)`: P.obligations() is [], P.eval("neg 2.0") returns -1.0, P.test("neg") reports 'neg: no laws'. The same type with `:= extern "python:operator.neg"` in the file gives P.obligations() == ['neg']. The test covers a top-level subtype (Sqrt) only.

behaviors.behavior: Bool is the alias `< true : Unit | false : Unit >`. A sum of two units with other labels converts to Bool, but `if` and laws require the labels true and false. A converted value prints with its own label (`yes : Bool`).
behaviors.spec_ref: 04-kernel.md:27-28 and 68-73 (labels are binders, not part of the type's identity); 05-static-semantics.md:21
behaviors.evidence: checker.py:125-131 (is_bool by labels), 1926-1931, 1009. `YesNo = < yes : Unit | no : Unit >\ny : YesNo := yes\nb : Bool := y` evaluates `b` to `yes : Bool`; `x : Int := if y then 1 else 2` gives `true is a label of Bool, and the value matched is of type < yes : Unit | no : Unit >: the condition of an if ... need a Bool`; `L (x : Int) : YesNo := yes`, `t : { x : Int | L x } := 3` gives `must be Bool-valued or a law`. The label rule was decided in docs/plan-2026-10-05.md:384 and never written into 04 or 05; test_checker_rules.py cites '(04)' for it.

behaviors.behavior: Between the constructors of a data and between the branches of a match, ';' is required except after the last. Without it the next constructor or pattern is parsed as an argument.
behaviors.spec_ref: 02-grammar.md:39 and 02-grammar.md:85 (`[ ";" ]`), with 02-grammar.md:27 (line breaks ignored inside match braces)
behaviors.evidence: parser.py:320-326 and 718-724. `f (b : Bool) : Int := match b {\n  true -> 1\n  false -> 0 }` gives `type error: in f: 1 : Int is not a function, cannot apply it to false`; `T : U := data { leaf : T node : T -> T -> T }` gives `expected 'name', got ':'`. A trailing ';' is accepted. The EBNF admits a derivation where ';' is optional, but the greedy application the precedence table implies does not, so the grammar is ambiguous on this point.

behaviors.behavior: Implicit parameters `{A : U}` count as positions of the clause tuple, so every clause must write a pattern for them.
behaviors.spec_ref: 02-grammar.md:51 (clauses are a match on the tuple of the parameters); 02-grammar.md:133-140 (implicit parameters)
behaviors.evidence: clauses_to_match collects names from all binders, implicit included. `len {A : U} (l : List A) : Int\n  | nil := 0\n  | cons x xs := 1 + len xs` gives `parse error: clause has 1 patterns but the header has 2 parameters`; it must be written `| _, nil := 0`. The spec does not say whether implicit parameters are in the tuple.

behaviors.behavior: Named products and sums written with * or + work with two positions only. With three, `(a : A) + (b : B) + (c : C)` is rejected with a wrong message, and `(a : A) * (b : B) * (c : C)` is accepted but loses its labels.
behaviors.evidence: parser.py:552-563: the right operand parse_binop(6) already returns a Sum or labeled product, not a Named. `S = (a : Int) + (b : Bool) + (c : String)` gives `every alternative of a named sum is written (label : Type)` (they all are). `P = (a : Int) * (b : Bool) * (c : String)` checks, but `p.a` gives `p : P has no named components` and `{ a := 1, b := true, c := "s" }` is rejected. Two positions work for both. No test covers the + form.

behaviors.behavior: A one-component labeled product `{ a : Int }` is built in the same form as a refinement, so it has no named component: projection, record literal and Program.record all fail.
behaviors.spec_ref: 02-grammar.md:78 (labeled product with one or more groups); 05-static-semantics.md:38-39 (labeled base); 02-grammar.md:117-118 (a refinement has the components of its base)
behaviors.evidence: labeled_product returns Subtype(PVar(n), t, NoLaw()) for one component (parser.py:781-783); checker.py:1107 walks through any subtype whose pattern is a single variable. `P = { a : Int }\np : P := 3` gives `p.a`: `p : P has no named components, so .a means nothing`; `p : P := { a := 3 }`: `a record literal needs a type with named components, not P`; luthier.load(...).record("one") raises KeyError. The spec is ambiguous between the two readings.

behaviors.behavior: Some number tokens the lexer accepts crash the parser with a Python traceback: a pattern `1e3` (int() on an exponent), and a test count or size that is not an integer (`with 1.5`, `with 1e2`). A negative literal pattern `-1` is a parse error.
behaviors.spec_ref: 02-grammar.md:14 (number includes decimals and exponents); 02-grammar.md:45 ("with" number); 02-grammar.md:94 (patom number)
behaviors.evidence: parser.py:758 `PLit(float(t.text) if "." in t.text else int(t.text))`; parser.py:126 and 132 `int(...)`. `k (x : Float64) : Int := match x { 1e3 -> 1 ; _ -> 0 }` makes `luthier check` print `Traceback ... ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '1e3'` (`1.0e3` works). `test sq with 1.5` gives `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '1.5'`. The loader catches only ParseError and LexError (cli.py:85-88).

behaviors.behavior: `test name [with n | exhaustive] [size k]` in that order; 100 cases when `with` is absent; `as`-style contextual word `size`. The richer directive of 08 (sampled, under, where, profile) is not parsed.
behaviors.spec_ref: 02-grammar.md:45; 08-tests.md:340-343 and 354-365 (new grammar and removal of gen: decided, listed as order of work, not implemented)
behaviors.evidence: Default n=100 at parser.py:123 and syntax.py:282 is not stated anywhere in the spec. `test sq size 3 with 10` gives `unexpected 'with' at end of definition`; `test sq with 10 sampled linear` gives `unexpected 'sampled'`; `profile tape := {...}` gives `unexpected 'tape'` (08 status: decided, pending). `test sq with 5 size 3` checks; no test exercises `size`.

behaviors.behavior: parse_term stops after the first complete term and ignores the rest, so `luthier eval` and Program.eval/term silently drop trailing tokens.
behaviors.evidence: parse_term never checks for eof; used by cli.py:576 and api.py:131. `luthier eval api_eval.lut "1 + 2 ) junk"` prints `3 : Int`; P.eval("a ]") returns 3.

behaviors.behavior: Lambda `\ p1 p2 { t }` with parameters a name, `(x y : T)` or a tuple pattern `(p, q)`; zero parameters are accepted (`\ { 3 }` is 3); `_` as a lambda parameter is an ordinary variable the body can use.
behaviors.evidence: `f : Int * Int * Int -> Int := \ (x, y, z) { x - y - z }` gives `f (9, 2, 3)` = 4; `luthier eval f.lut "\ { 3 }"` prints `3 : Int` though the grammar needs one lparam; `f : Int -> Int := \ _ { _ }` gives `f 7` = 7 while `match x { _ -> _ }` is `unbound name _`. No test or library uses the tuple-pattern parameter.

behaviors.behavior: `forget atom` gives the base value of a subtype; on a non-subtype it is an error.
behaviors.evidence: `Pos : U := { x : Int | x > 0 }\np : Pos := 3\nq : Int := forget p + 1` gives q = 4; `forget 3` gives `forget applied to 3 : Int, which is not a subtype`. No test and no library uses forget.

behaviors.behavior: A hole filled from Python is an extern whose fingerprint is the constant "filled", so refilling it with another function keeps it certified in the session; across sessions certificates are compared at load, before any fill, so a Python-filled hole is never accepted from its certificate.
behaviors.spec_ref: 05-static-semantics.md:320-326 (the hash covers the Python behind every extern; the comparison happens once holes are filled; one entry per filling); 03-libraries.md:241-244
behaviors.evidence: certify.py:246 maps non-python targets to "filled"; api.py:120-126 only removes entries. Probe api_refill.lut (root : Sqrt): fill math.sqrt, test passes; fill `lambda x: 0.0`: definition_hash unchanged, 'root' still in checker.certified, loader.stale == []. New session: load, fill math.sqrt, 'root' not certified and test(deep=False) reruns.

behaviors.behavior: Program.eval types the term silently, still checks closed coercions, and raises HoleBlocked when the term needs a hole without a value (the docstring says a stuck term comes back).
behaviors.spec_ref: 05-static-semantics.md:308-310 (run and eval require every name in the cone to be defined)
behaviors.evidence: `h : Int\ng (x : Int) : Int := x + h`: P.eval("g 1") raises `HoleBlocked: depends on h without a value`, as does `luthier eval ... "g 1"`. `use (x : Pos)`: P.eval("use 0") raises `TypeCheckError: 0 does not satisfy Pos`. No test covers an eval blocked by a hole.

behaviors.behavior: Program.call converts each Python argument by the base of its parameter's declared type and does not check its refinement. Too many arguments raise 'takes fewer than N arguments'.
behaviors.spec_ref: 06-numbers.md:103 (a value is checked against its declared type when it crosses)
behaviors.evidence: `Pos : U := { x : Int | x > 0 }\nuse (x : Pos) : Int := x * 10`: P.call("use", -3) returns -30 and `idx (k : Small)` with Small = 0..2 gives P.call("idx", 7) = 7, while P.eval("use 0") raises `0 does not satisfy Pos`. P.call("g", 1, 2) raises `EvalError: g takes fewer than 2 arguments`. call has no test.

behaviors.behavior: The rest of the Python API: holes() lists bodiless non-core definitions, type holes only with include_types; definitions(), obligations() (top files first), blocked_by() (holes in the cone, type parameters), record() (dataclass of a type with named components, KeyError otherwise), test_all(), term(), resolve() (KeyError 'no definition').
behaviors.evidence: Probes: holes() == [] and holes(include_types=True) == ['Session']; blocked_by("a") == {'holes': ['k'], 'types': []}; record("Pt")(1.0, 2.0) == Pt(x=1.0, y=2.0); record("Q") on Float64 * Float64 raises KeyError 'Q has no named components'. Only holes() and the dataclass crossing are tested; definitions, obligations, blocked_by, record, test_all and term have no test.

behaviors.behavior: List constructors take the element type as an explicit first argument (`cons Int 1 (nil Int)`); the implicit-parameter inference does not apply to them. A list literal without an expected type is rejected with a message that says a first element would do.
behaviors.spec_ref: 04-kernel.md:161 (`[a, b, c]` is `cons a (cons b (cons c nil))`, element type from the expected type)
behaviors.evidence: `xs : List Int := cons 1 nil` gives `type error: in xs: 1 has type Int but U was expected`; `cons Int 1 (nil Int)` works and is how literals print. `luthier eval f.lut "[1, 2]"` gives `error: a list literal needs an expected type or a first element`, though it has a first element.

behaviors.behavior: ExtendedReal = < finite : Float64 | negInf : Unit | posInf : Unit >.
behaviors.evidence: `e : ExtendedReal := negInf` evaluates to `negInf : ExtendedReal`. No test and no library under src/luthier/lib uses it.

behaviors.behavior: A name may start with '_', may end in '#digits' (x#1 is a name distinct from x), '_' alone is a name token, and only ASCII letters are allowed.
behaviors.evidence: `_hidden : Int := 3\nx#2 : Int := _hidden + 1` evaluates `x#2` to 4; `x#1 : Int := 1\nx : Int := 2` evaluates `x#1 + x` to 3. The '#digits' suffix is used nowhere else in src. `π : Float64 := 3.14` gives `unexpected character 'π'`.

behaviors.behavior: `let`, `in`, `primitive` and `axiom` are reserved, though 02 §1 does not list them; `as` and `size` are contextual and usable as names.
behaviors.evidence: `in : Int := 3` gives `parse error: line 1, col 0: expected 'name', got 'in'`; same for let, axiom, primitive. `as : Int := 3\nsize : Int := as + 1` evaluates to 4. 02 §7 added let/in and 04 §1:45 added primitive/axiom without updating the list.

behaviors.behavior: A number with '.' or an exponent is a Float64 literal, otherwise an unbounded Int (`1e3` is 1000.0 : Float64, rejected where Int is expected).
behaviors.evidence: `x : Float64 := 1e3` evaluates to `1000.0 : Float64`; `x : Int := 1e3` gives `1000.0 has type Float64 but Int was expected`. The spec does not say how an exponent literal is typed.

behaviors.behavior: An unknown character is `parse error: line L, col C: unexpected character 'X'` with columns from 0; after a string literal that spans a line break, reported lines are one too low; the tokens '{ and ${ exist and no rule uses them.
behaviors.evidence: `x : Int := 3 @ 4` gives `line 1, col 13: unexpected character '@'`. `s : String := "a\nb"` (raw newline) followed by `x : Int := (1 + )` on line 3 reports `line 2, col 16`: lines advance only on newline tokens (lexer.py:49-58). `x : Int := ${ 3 }` gives `expected a term (at '${')`.

behaviors.behavior: `--` starts a comment to the end of the line, also right after a token (`x --2` is `x`).
behaviors.evidence: `y : Int := x --2` evaluates to the value of x. Every tests/spec file begins with comment lines and its `-- expect:` comment.

behaviors.behavior: An act starts at column 0 and an indented line continues it; a clause line must be indented; inside record type braces a line break ends a component, so a component type spans lines only inside parentheses.
behaviors.evidence:
`x : Int :=
  1 +
  2` gives 3; `x : Int :=
1 + 2` gives `expected a term (at '
')`; a clause `| zero := zero` at column 0 gives `expected 'name', got '|'`; `P = { f : Int ->
  Int, b : Bool }` fails, `{ f : (Int ->
  Int), b : Bool }` checks.

behaviors.behavior: `gen T := term` or `gen T := extern "..."`; `extern provisional` is rejected in this position though it is a term elsewhere.
behaviors.evidence: `gen P := extern provisional "python:x.y"` gives `expected 'string', got 'provisional'`. The act is still parsed, as 08 §13 lists its removal as work to do.

behaviors.behavior: `import "path" [as name]`; the path must be a string; a dotted alias (`as a.b`) is accepted.
behaviors.evidence: `import real` gives `expected 'string', got 'real'`; `import "real" as a.b` checks; `import "nope_such_file"` gives `cannot find import 'nope_such_file'`.

behaviors.behavior: Declaration, definition and alias; binders `(x y : A)` wrap the type in Pi and the body in lambdas; the type is optional (`x := 4` with no declaration is accepted); bodies may be data, extern [provisional], primitive or axiom; a bare name is 'definition 'x' needs a type or a body'.
behaviors.evidence: `f (x y : Int) (z : Int) : Int := x + y + z` gives f 1 2 3 = 6; `x := 4` evaluates to 4. The `body` rule of 02 §2 omits primitive and axiom, which 04 §1:45 and parser.py:225-230 have.

behaviors.behavior: Implicit binders `{A B : U}` only before the explicit ones; on an alias the braces are accepted and the parameter is simply explicit.
behaviors.evidence: `f (x : Int) {A : U} : Int := x` gives `unexpected '{' at end of definition`; `Pair2 {A : U} = A * A` checks with no implicit effect (parser.py:198-206 ignores the count). parser.py:305 defines _binder_ahead and parser.py:583 redefines it; the first is dead.

behaviors.behavior: Precedence & -> or and comparisons + - * / mod application; & and -> to the right, the others to the left. `and` and `or` are core functions usable prefix; `mod` is a primitive operator, not a name: `mod 7 3` is unbound and a user definition named mod is ignored by infix mod.
behaviors.spec_ref: 02-grammar.md:58-65; 02-grammar.md:22-23 (and, or and mod are ordinary names written infix)
behaviors.evidence: `10 - 3 - 2` = 5; `and true false` = false; `luthier eval f.lut "mod 7 3"` gives `unbound name mod`; with `mod (a b : Int) : Int := 42`, `7 mod 3` is still 1. `1 < 2 < 3` is rejected by type.

behaviors.behavior: Unary minus binds looser than application: `-f 3` is -(f 3); `f -3` is f - 3; the checker makes it 0 - x or 0.0 - x.
behaviors.evidence: `-f 3` = -4 with f x = x + 1; `f -3` gives `operator - expects Int, Float64 or Rational, got f`; `- -3` = 3; a user `__negate__` definition does not change `-3`.

behaviors.behavior: `let p = e in body` is a one-branch match; any pattern parses, a refutable one is rejected by the checker.
behaviors.evidence: `let (p, q) = (2, 3) in p * q` = 6; `let just y = m in y` gives `match on m does not cover: nothing`.

behaviors.behavior: `if c then a else b` is a match on the labels true and false.
behaviors.evidence: `if 2 < 3 then 1 else 0` = 1; `f if true then 1 else 2` parses as an argument. See CORE-2 for the condition's type.

behaviors.behavior: `[a, b]` becomes a cons/nil chain elaborated by the checker; a trailing comma is accepted; without commas `[1 2]` is the one-element list `[(1 2)]`.
behaviors.evidence: `xs : List Int := [1, 2,]` evaluates to `cons Int 1 (cons Int 2 (nil Int))`; `[1 2]` gives `1 : Int is not a function, cannot apply it to 2`. User definitions named __nil__ or __cons__ do not change literals.

behaviors.behavior: `extern [provisional] "target"` is a term, typed by context, but it cannot be an unparenthesized argument.
behaviors.evidence: `p : P := { f := extern "python:builtins.abs", g := 2 }` works; `y : Int := app extern "python:builtins.abs" 3` gives `unexpected 'extern' at end of definition` (starts_atom, parser.py:387-399, excludes extern).

behaviors.behavior: `(x y : A) -> B`, `(x y : A) * B`, tuples `(a, b, c)` nested to the right; `(x : A)` alone is an error from the checker, `(a b : Int)` alone a parse error.
behaviors.evidence: `P = (x y : Int) * { k : Int | x < k and k < y }\np : P := (1, 5, 3)` checks; `P = (a b : Int)` gives `expected '->', '*' or '+' after a dependent binder`; `P = (a : Int)` gives `(a : Int) names a position of a product or a sum`.

behaviors.behavior: `{ a b : A, c : B }` is a labeled product and `{ ... | p }` a subtype over the dependent product of its components; groups are separated by ',', ';' or a line break.
behaviors.evidence:
`P = { a : Int

output.notes:
Answer to Luciano for this slice (front end: lexer, parser, syntax tree, printer, Python API, core.lut). The grammar in 02 is close to the parser but not faithful: 12 behaviors are high. Nine are in the grammar and core: a closing bracket at column 0 is rejected (LAY-1), a line break between record-value fields fails (LAY-3), the clause form contradicts the definition rule (GRAM-2), `{ pattern : T | p }` is not parsed (GRAM-4), parentheses around * and + types are lost (GRAM-5), a union cannot contain '>' (GRAM-6), `operator` accepts any symbol and lets == bypass R8 (GRAM-9), Bool is told by labels contrary to 04 (CORE-2), and `1e400` is accepted as an infinite Float64 (LEX-4). One is in the lexer and parser: non-ASCII string literals are corrupted, and pattern strings are decoded differently from term strings (LEX-5). Two are in the Python API, which no spec section describes: fill does not apply R5 or R2 (API-3), and does not raise R5's codomain or component obligations (API-4). No test exercises any of them. The README example (copied to scratch) checks and evaluates as documented.

Commit: HEAD is 58dd490, one commit after b15f2a1; `git diff b15f2a1 HEAD` is empty for src, docs/semantica, tests, README.md and examples, so the findings hold for b15f2a1.

Method: every probe is a small program under /tmp/claude-1000/-home-lmoffatt-Projects-luthier/8d5ce152-b54e-48c4-a388-e7a9ccb80792/scratchpad/audit/impl-front/ (probe.py runs `luthier check` or `luthier eval` on each case; api_probe.py, api_refill.lut and capture.lut exercise the API and the printer). Nothing in the repository was modified and luthier certify was not run.

Declared statuses respected: 08 §12-13 (test directive with sampled/under/where, `profile` act, removal of `gen`) are decided and listed as work to do, so the parser still having the old forms is reported as that status (GRAM-10, GRAM-12). 02 §8 open items (quote and unquote, local `{ x := t ; u }` blocks, saved evaluation) are not parsed, which is consistent. R11 is declared not implemented and is outside this scope.

Internal behaviors, listed only here: syntax.py dataclasses and fields (Def.doc is always empty, Def.pending, Program.find); parser placeholders __negate__, __cons__, __nil__ (user definitions with those names do not hijack them); _is_con_name always returns False; the duplicate _binder_ahead (parser.py:305 shadowed by 583); no_brace for match scrutinees; pretty.py helpers (_labeled_components, _projected_name, over-parenthesized left operands of left-associative operators); api.py _from_core, _refresh_certificates, the `filled` dict.

Observed outside this scope, for the other auditors: (1) evaluator: printing the normal form of an unapplied function substitutes a global for a pattern variable of the same name. With `a : Int := 1`, `luthier eval capture.lut \"\\ (p : Int * Int) { match p { (a, _) -> a } }\"` prints `match p { (a, _) -> 1 }`, though applying it gives 5. (2) checker: `\"a\" + \"b\"` concatenates Strings and `\"a\" < \"b\"` is rejected, while 04 §4 lists comparisons on String literals; Int `/` floors (`(-7) / 2` = -4) and `mod` follows Python's sign, neither specified. (3) checker: with `operator + := addP` over a one-component record, `+` on Int inside addP resolves to addP and the error reads 'its body has type something else'. (4) README.md:73 says rules R1 to R8; 05 has R1 to R11.

Severity notes: GRAM-1 is medium, not high, because the EBNF with `[ \";\" ]` is ambiguous under greedy application, so it does not plainly accept the program. GRAM-7 and GRAM-8 are medium because the spec shows only two positions, and its refinement rule (02 §6) collides with a one-component record.
